newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on central bank news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on central bank news.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday following the central bank's comment that the local currency has no room to depreciate sharply, dealers said.
The Taiwan dollar ended at T$27.538 against Tuesday's T$27.545 close. Turnover was an active US$275 million.

A central bank official said earlier on Wednesday that the Taiwan dollar's comparison indices against other major foreign currencies had declined since early 1996, indicating there was no room for the local unit to depreciate sharply.
"The central bank comment prompted early buying of the local currency, but the local dollar also has limited room to rise," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
In recent weeks the Taiwan dollar had been in a downtrend against the American currency, reflecting the greenback's overseas strength against the yen and other currencies.
The market is closed on Thursday for a national holiday. Trading resumes on Friday.
Dealers expected consolidatory trading for Friday's session with a range of T$27.52-56 range seen.
